result.keyDetails:
ENDPOINT: POST /api/chat/stream (router mounted under prefix /api/chat in backend/main.py; the explicit /stream subpath avoids the 307 redirect that a bare POST /api/chat without trailing slash gets against the existing root handler). Confirmed via curl -i that no 307 is returned.

REQUEST BODY (new pydantic model ChatStreamRequest):
{
  "messages": [ { "role": "user"|"assistant", "content": "string" }, ... ],  // reuses existing ChatMessage model (role: str, content: str)
  "ticker": null | "string",       // optional, default null
  "max_results": 10                 // optional int, default 10
}
Query = content of the LAST message in `messages` with role=="user". History = all OTHER messages (excludes that one query message by index, not just ones before it), capped to the most recent 10, rendered as one line each "User: <content>" / "Assistant: <content>", in original order, joined with \\n.

PRE-STREAM ERRORS (plain HTTP, not SSE): 400 {"detail": "No user message found in messages"} if no role=="user" message exists; 502 {"detail": "Retrieval failed"} if embedding/vector-search raised (real exception is logger.error'd server-side only, never leaked to the client).

RESPONSE: StreamingResponse, media_type="text/event-stream", headers {"Cache-Control":"no-cache","X-Accel-Buffering":"no"}. Every SSE frame is `event: <name>\\n` then exactly one `data: <json>\\n\\n` line; json.dumps uses separators=(',',':') and default=str so no embedded newlines.

SSE EVENTS in order:
1. event: sources -- emitted exactly once, first, always (even when sources is an empty array). data: {"sources": [ ...enriched source objects... ]}
   Enriched source object fields (exact names): document_id, chunk_id, title, url, source_name, published_at, tickers, classification, similarity, excerpt. title/url/source_name/published_at come from a single batched `documents` table select (columns id,title,url,source_name,published_at) via .in_('id', [...ids]); on a lookup miss/failure those 4 fields degrade to null (JSON null) for that source rather than erroring. tickers/classification/similarity/excerpt/chunk_id come from the retrieved chunk metadata (chunk_id was newly added to SimpleRetriever's metadata dict as result.get('chunk_id')). excerpt = doc.page_content[:200] + "...".
2. event: delta -- zero or more (one per streamed token from ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", streaming=True).astream). data: {"text": "..."}
   Special case: if retrieval returned zero documents, exactly one delta event is sent with the SAME canned text the JSON POST / handler uses: "I couldn't find any relevant information in the database to answer your question. Try asking about specific tickers or legal issues." -- no LLM call is made in that path.
3. terminal event (exactly one, last): either event: done with data: {"finish_reason": "stop"}, OR event: error with data: {"message": "<generic string, e.g. 'The assistant encountered an error while generating a response.'>"} on a mid-stream exception -- the message is always a fixed, generic string, never str(e).

Context assembly for the LLM prompt (inside the new RAG_PROMPT_WITH_HISTORY.format(history=..., context=..., question=...) call) is byte-identical in format to the existing POST / handler's loop: "[Source {i+1}] Tickers: {tickers}\\nClassification: {classification}\\nContent: {content}" joined by "\\n\\n---\\n\\n", enumerate(relevant_docs) order -- so "[Source N]" citations the model produces line up 1:1 with sources[N-1] in the sources event.

NEW SYMBOLS added to backend/routes/chat.py (all additive, nothing else touched): pydantic model `ChatStreamRequest`; PromptTemplate `RAG_PROMPT_WITH_HISTORY` (input_variables=["history","context","question"]; existing RAG_PROMPT is untouched, still input_variables=["context","question"]); async helper `_enrich_sources(supabase, documents) -> List[dict]`; helper `_sse_event(event: str, data: dict) -> str`; route handler `async def chat_stream(request: ChatStreamRequest)` registered via `@router.post(\"/stream\")`. SimpleRetriever.aget_relevant_documents's metadata dict now also includes 'chunk_id': result.get('chunk_id') (the only edit inside SimpleRetriever; RPC call, match_threshold=0.7, and ranking are unchanged).
